results.title: Google's Fitbit Edge Sits Between a Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5
results.content:
You may have already seen the Fitbit Edge back when the Fitbit Air launched because Google strangely included it in marketing materials but then stayed tight-lipped on what it was. The $179.99 wearable launches on Oct. 27 (pre-orders start today, Oct. 12) and offers a little of both the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. You could also view it as the successor to the Fitbit Charge 6.

So what do you get? Basically all of the fitness and heart tracking that the Fitbit Air has and a few extra features like a clock, GPS, and, of course, a 1.34-inch OLED screen for showing stuff like Google Map routes, notifications, weather, and music controls.

# Google's Fitbit Edge Sits Between a Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5

You can also think of the Fitbit Air as the successor to the Fitbit Charge 6.

By    Raymond Wong

Reading time 3 minutes

Fitbit Edge 1

Google really wants to sell a health and fitness wearable to every possible consumer. If you want one of the best Android-based smartwatches there is, get a Pixel Watch 5. Don't want a screen or notifications on your wrist? There's the Fitbit Air. And now, Google has a hybrid wearable that sits in between those two: the Fitbit Edge.

results.title: Forget the Fitbit Air — 5 things you need to know about the rumored Fitbit Edge | Tom's Guide
results.content:
While 2026's Fitbit Air is in some ways the spiritual successor to the Fitbit Charge 6, the lack of a screen, smart features, and onboard GPS means it doesn't quite fill the same shoes as its older sibling.

So, will Google ever launch a Charge 6 replacement, or is the brand too concerned about sales potentially cannibalizing interest in the Pixel Watch 5? Based on a host of recent rumors and links, the former now seems likely.

That's right, a true-blue Fitbit Charge 6 replacement could debut as early as this year. Better yet, it may combine all the best bits of the Fitbit Charge 6 in a smaller, more Fitbit Air-like package.

Here are the five biggest things you should know about the rumored Fitbit Edge. [...] a photo of the screen on the Fitbit Charge 6

The Fitbit Air is $99, while the Fitbit Charge 6 launched at $159. How much can we expect the Fitbit Edge to go for? Given the rate of inflation over the past three years, it seems likely that the Edge will cost a little bit more than its predecessor, but I highly doubt it will surpass $200.

What are your thoughts on the Fitbit Edge? Does it sound like a proper replacement for the Fitbit Charge 6? Moreover, cost aside, which fitness tracker would you rather own, the screen-free Fitbit Air or a screen- and GPS-equipped Fitbit Edge? Let me know below.

results.title: The best Fitbit alternatives of 2026: Fitness trackers, smartwatches and more
results.content:
The Google Pixel Watch 4 is the best Fitbit alternative for anyone who wants the best of both worlds: the wellness insights of Fitbit and the powerful smarts of Wear OS. Technically, it's still a Fitbit, just one packed into premium hardware and powered by Google's full smartwatch platform. Simply put, it blows the Fitbit's older smartwatch lineups out of the water. I've tested every Pixel Watch to date, and thanks to useful upgrades and refinements, the 4 feels like the most complete version yet. For users who want real fitness tracking alongside true smartwatch features, it's the most well-rounded option available. [...] The Pixel Watch line is the main reason Fitbit's older models have fallen by the wayside. Google continually kneecapped the Sense and Versa lines to direct shoppers to its premium offering, and as a result, Pixel Watches are the only smartwatches worth buying under the Fitbit umbrella. Yet what sets the device apart from Fitbit's past is the unique blend of Fitbit's health tracking and Google's app ecosystem. You still get access to core Fitbit features like sleep and activity tracking, heart rate monitoring, and Fitbit Premium insights, but now they're bundled with all the best of Google's toolkit. For everything else, the Google Play Store offers an extensive library of apps and watch faces. [...] Health and fitness features remain strengths of the Galaxy Watch lineup, with ample workout features and everything from skin temperature to enhanced sleep tracking. While Samsung Health doesn't offer quite the same level of granularity as Garmin, for most users, especially those focused on general wellness, it strikes a nice balance between functionality and simplicity, making it a solid Fitbit alternative. As with previous models, the Galaxy Watch 8 also taps into full access to the Play Store, Google Assistant, Wallet, Maps, and more, giving the watch a distinct edge over Fitbit devices in terms of versatility and app support.

If you're in the Samsung ecosystem, the Galaxy Watch 8 offers everything Fitbit does plus unique integration.

results.title: Google Fitbit Edge vs Fitbit Air: Which should you choose? | Tom's Guide
results.content:
I'm yet to test the Fitbit Edge, but will, of course, be following up with a full review once I get my hands on one. The Fitbit Air, on the other hand, is one of my favorite fitness trackers of 2026.

Part of the appeal when it comes to the Fitbit Air is its low cost and its comfortable design. For $99, you're getting an excellent fitness tracker that's seriously comfortable. However, you obviously can't see any live feedback during your workouts.

The Fitbit Edge seems to be in the middle. It won't give you all the notifications and apps as the Pixel Watch 5, but it will give you more than the Fitbit Air, which doesn't have a screen, an ECG app, or built-in GPS.

Unlike the Google Pixel Watch 5, the Fitbit Edge will work with Android and iOS. [...] But where does it fit in Google's smartwatch lineup? And should you choose the Fitbit Edge or the $99 Fitbit Air? Read on to find out more
